A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSLoRA research, with matching objectives, algorithms, and benchmark experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite the revised title and appendix organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments on GLUE, commonsense reasoning, and LLaMA-7B instruction-tuning datasets, including benchmark comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds sketch-selection comparisons, gradient statistics, local-update ablations, and dynamic-resource simulations.

M1.justification: The core sketching objective, update equations, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v3 explicitly extends sketching sets to time-varying sparsity in Appendix H.3 and describes a client-subsampling extension in Appendix F. These are limited procedural extensions, without a redesigned core algorithm.

E1.justification: The datasets and language tasks are retained, including the LLaMA-7B experiments previously in Appendix D and now in G. Appendix H.3 adds a distinct simulated environment with time-varying client resources, extending the earlier static resource scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table C.1 compares random-k sketching against two importance-based alternatives using products or sums of component norms. The existing benchmark comparator sets are unchanged: FedStackLoRA in v2 is renamed FLoRA in v3.

E3.justification: The reported default LLaMA-3.2-3B training budget changes from 500 to 200 communication rounds, with corresponding plot-axis revisions. Section 5.2 and Figure 3(a) change its upload budget from 200× to 80×, although Appendix H.1 and Figure 5 retain 200×. New experiments vary local updates and resource dynamics. These materially revise documented protocols without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix C tests random versus importance-based sketch selection; E examines gradient magnitudes underlying assumptions; H.2 varies local updates; and H.3 compares static and dynamic sketching ratios. The earlier rank, sketching, heterogeneity, and compression analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E introduces gradient estimation across four clients and reports minimum and maximum estimated expected norms over 30 randomly sampled model states. This adds a statistical sampling and summarization procedure. Table 5.1 retains its three independent runs and unchanged uncertainty values; no increase in training runs is established.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark tables are numerically unchanged. New results include importance-sketching averages of 73.2 and 74.2 against random-k's 79.1, static/dynamic averages of 79.3/79.0, gradient statistics, and local-update curves. Reported accuracy-versus-round coordinates also change, and the compression plot uses a tenfold smaller MB scale in v3 Figure 8 than v2 Figure 7. These do not establish gains under identical settings.

T1.justification: v3 adds a sparse-mask cancellation derivation for aggregation in Appendix D and gradient variance/dissimilarity bounds in E. The existing convergence assumptions, rate, and proof mathematics are retained. Combining v2 Theorem 4.4 and Corollary 4.5 into v3 Theorem 4.4 is principally reorganization, including a step-size condition already present in v2's appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: resource-adaptive sketching of global LoRA modules, convergence guarantees depending on sketching ratios, and empirical efficiency and accuracy advantages. Replacing on-device terminology with client-side terminology does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for importance-based sketching's weaker performance, interprets gradient statistics as support for its assumptions, and discusses diminishing benefits from additional local updates and applicability to dynamic resources. It removes v2's explicit limitation concerning the absence of real-device deployment, without adding such a study.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies sampling ten clients per round for the retained 50/100-client experiments, without establishing a change from their actual earlier implementation. It also documents dynamic ratio ranges, gradient sampling, and compression operations more explicitly, and states that code accompanies the supplementary material. The public code URL and hardware disclosure remain.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 replaces its centralized LoRA-extension discussion with a substantial sketching-based optimization discussion, positioning FSLoRA relative to regression, distributed sketching, and privacy research. Added works include Charalambides and Mazumdar, Shrivastava et al., and Nicolas et al.; removed works include SLTrain, ReLoRA, and two chain-LoRA approaches.

P1.justification: The title and portions of the introduction are rewritten, and device/on-device terminology is broadly replaced with client/federated terminology. Appendix sections are reorganized, implementation details precede proofs, and theorem/corollary presentation is consolidated. The overall main-text section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables C.1, E.1, and H.1 and a local-update Figure 7; the existing compression plot becomes Figure 8. Retained plots receive revised legends and round/MB axes, and appendix figures and tables move. The main visual design and most display structures remain.

improvement.justification: The new sketch-selection, local-update, and dynamic-resource analyses strengthen the paper's supporting evidence. However, v3 introduces conflicting 80×/200× budgets for corresponding results, changes the compression plot's MB scale without explaining the revision, and removes the deployment limitation without deployment evidence. These issues affect the central efficiency claims, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
